$comment: The app's rendered output for each input below, written by scripts/render-contract-golden.mjs from the live renderer (src/app/components/rendered-text/) under jsdom, with the configuration render-contract.json publishes. Regenerate it with that script; never edit it by hand.

src/app/components/rendered-text/render-contract.spec.ts re-renders every input, directly and through RenderedTextComponent, and fails on any difference, and on a generatedWith that no longer names the installed packages — so a change to the renderer, or to marked, KaTeX, DOMPurify, jsdom or the parse5 jsdom serialises with, is a change to this file in the same pull request.

A renderer configured from render-contract.json reproduces every output here byte for byte, or it is not the app's renderer. block renders a question and its explanation; inline renders an answer option. katex says whether render-contract.json's math.selection pattern matched the input, so it rendered through the instance with the KaTeX renderer, as the app would; false means the instance without one, which is where most questions go.

output is the string the renderer returns — DOMPurify's serialisation, which the app writes into an element as it is — and it is jsdom's serialisation: parse5, at the version under generatedWith. A browser builds the same DOM but need not write it the same way: Chromium 141 escapes < and > inside an attribute value (title="a<b>c") where parse5 writes them as they are (title="a<b>c"), as link-title-with-angle-brackets shows. Byte equality is defined under jsdom; compare there.
A case whose about starts 'Known defect' records the renderer as it behaves today, not as it should: a fix changes that output, and the change shows here.

cases.name: plain-question
cases.about: Text with no Markdown in it: one paragraph.
cases.input: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
cases.output: Which planet is closest to the Sun?

cases.name: plain-answer
cases.about: An answer option carrying characters HTML reads: escaped, with no wrapper element.

cases.name: currency-is-not-math
cases.about: Two prices are not a formula: the inline delimiter refuses whitespace before its closing $, so the source takes the instance without KaTeX.

cases.name: character-references
cases.about: marked passes references through; the parse DOMPurify does decodes them and the serialiser re-escapes only what HTML needs.

cases.name: emphasis-and-code
cases.about: strong, em, del (GFM) and an inline code span.

cases.name: paragraphs-and-line-breaks
cases.about: Two trailing spaces and a trailing backslash are hard breaks (br); a bare newline is a soft one and stays a newline (breaks: false).
cases.input:
First line  
second line\
third line
same paragraph

Next paragraph.
cases.output:
First line
second line
third line same paragraph

Next paragraph.

cases.name: blockquote
cases.about: A quote, with a mark inside it.

cases.name: lists
cases.about: A bulleted list with a nested one, then a numbered list.

cases.name: https-links
cases.about: An https link keeps its href and title and is given target and rel; a bare https URL is a GFM autolink and gets the same.
cases.output: MDN and https://example.org/page

cases.name: uppercase-https-link
cases.about: The hook parses the href rather than prefix-matching it: an uppercase scheme is https: all the same, so the link keeps its href and gains target and rel. A port that compares strings drops it.

cases.name: link-title-with-angle-brackets
cases.about: jsdom (parse5) writes < and > inside an attribute value as they are; Chromium writes < and >, the same DOM serialised differently. This file is jsdom's serialisation, so byte equality is defined there.

cases.name: fence-with-language
cases.about: The one class anything may carry: the fence language.

cases.name: fence-without-language
cases.about: A fence with no info string: a code block with no class.

cases.name: indented-code-block
cases.about: Renders byte for byte as fence-without-language. Only marked's token tells them apart — type code with codeBlockStyle 'indented' and no lang, against a fence's lang of '' — so a check that a fence names its language has to read the tokens, not this HTML.

cases.name: unclosed-fence
cases.about: A fence that is never closed runs to the end of the source and is a code block, not an error.

cases.name: unbalanced-emphasis
cases.about: Emphasis that never closes is not emphasis: the asterisks stay as text.

cases.name: inline-math
cases.about: A $…$ formula in a sentence: MathML with no display attribute. The GFM strikethrough beside it holds the block instance with KaTeX to gfm by its output.

cases.name: display-math
cases.about: A $$…$$ formula on its own lines: a block of its own, display="block", no paragraph.

cases.name: display-math-mid-sentence
cases.about: A $$…$$ formula inside a paragraph is still displayed in block mode. The newline before it is marked's: the paragraph is cut at the block extension's start marker and joined back with one.

cases.name: boxed-cancel-strike
cases.about: menclose and its notation attribute — the element whose absence once rendered \boxed{x} as x.
cases.output: x+y+z\boxed{x} + \cancel{y} + \sout{z}

cases.name: fractions-roots-scripts
cases.about: mfrac, mroot and msqrt; msubsup for a prescript, which KaTeX writes as scripts on an empty mrow rather than as mmultiscripts; msubsup again for the sum, whose limits stay scripts in inline style; msub.

cases.name: limits-under-and-over
cases.about: In display style a sum with both limits is munderover and a limit with one is munder; \underline is munder with accentunder.

cases.name: cases-environment
cases.about: mtable, mtr and mtd with their alignment and spacing attributes.
cases.output: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mo fence="true">{</mo><mtable rowspacing="0.36em" columnalign="left left" columnspacing="1em"><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>a</mi></mstyle></mtd><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>b</mi></mstyle></mtd><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mstyle></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{cases} a & x < 0 \\ b & x \ge 0 \end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math>

cases.name: array-with-rules
cases.about: An array with a vertical rule and an \hline: columnlines and rowlines.
cases.output: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mtable rowspacing="0.16em" columnalign="center center" columnlines="solid" columnspacing="1em" rowlines="solid"><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>a</mi></mstyle></mtd><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>b</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>c</mi></mstyle></mtd><mtd><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mi>d</mi></mstyle></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{array}{c|c} a & b \\ \hline c & d \end{array}</annotation></semantics></math>

cases.name: delimiters-accents-fonts
cases.about: Stretchy fences, an over-brace, an accent, a blackboard letter, a text run and an operator name.

cases.name: binomial-fences-spacing
cases.about: linethickness (\binom), minsize and maxsize (\big), separator (the comma in an argument list), lspace and rspace (\mathbin).
cases.output: (nk)(f(a,b))+x\binom{n}{k} \big( f(a, b) \big) \mathbin{+} x

cases.name: phantom-smash-small-integral
cases.about: mphantom, depth (\smash) and largeop (\smallint, the one operator KaTeX marks).

cases.name: math-inside-code
cases.about: A delimiter inside a code span or a fence is code: the fence tokenizer claims it first. The source still takes the KaTeX instance — the selection pattern reads the raw text — and nothing is compiled.

cases.name: heading
cases.about: A heading is not on the list: the tag goes, its words stay.

cases.name: image
cases.about: An image is not on the list, and an img has no text to keep: the alt text goes with it.

cases.name: table
cases.about: Known defect, recorded as the app renders it today: table elements are not on the list and their text is kept — except the header row, which DOMPurify drops whole, because thead is in its FORBID_CONTENTS.

cases.name: horizontal-rule
cases.about: A thematic break is not on the list and has no text: it goes.

cases.name: task-list
cases.about: A GFM task item keeps its text and loses its checkbox.

cases.name: links-that-are-not-https
cases.about: http, a relative path, mailto: and javascript: lose their href, and so does a www autolink, which marked gives http://: each anchor stays as its label.

cases.name: raw-html
cases.about: marked's html and tag tokenizers are off: raw HTML is text, escaped before DOMPurify sees it.

cases.name: event-handler-injection
cases.about: An injection attempt: the img and its handler arrive as escaped text.

cases.name: markup-inside-math
cases.about: Markup inside a formula is TeX to KaTeX: its characters become MathML operators and identifiers.

cases.name: katex-parse-error
cases.about: A formula that will not compile: KaTeX emits a span with an inline style, which the sanitiser drops while keeping the source text.

cases.name: katex-colour-and-rule
cases.about: mathcolor and mathbackground are a style attribute in MathML clothing: both go, and the rule keeps the space it reserves.

cases.name: katex-untrusted-command
cases.about: KaTeX runs untrusted (trust: false): \href compiles as an unsupported command, shown as text with its error colour stripped.

cases.name: known-overset-emptied
cases.about: Known defect, recorded as the app renders it today: KaTeX nests the over-script inside an <mo>, a MathML token element whose children the HTML parser puts in the HTML namespace; DOMPurify refuses a MathML name there and drops it with its content, so "a =! b" reads "ab".

cases.name: known-nested-token-constructs
cases.about: Known defect, recorded as the app renders it today: the same nesting empties \underset, \stackrel and \mathop…\limits: each leaves an empty token element behind.

cases.name: known-sizing-and-linebreak
cases.about: Known defect, recorded as the app renders it today: KaTeX emits mathsize for a sizing command and linebreak for \\, and neither is on the attribute list, so the size and the break are both lost.

cases.name: known-ordered-list-start
cases.about: Known defect, recorded as the app renders it today: marked writes start="3", which is not on the attribute list, so the list is numbered from 1.

cases.name: inline-link-as-label
cases.about: A link inside a button is nested interactive content: it renders as its formatted label.

cases.name: inline-display-math
cases.about: A $$…$$ formula in an answer compiles undisplayed.

cases.name: inline-block-syntax
cases.about: parseInline: list, quote and heading syntax stay as characters.

cases.name: inline-marks-and-math
cases.about: What an answer can carry: marks, GFM strikethrough among them, code and inline math — which takes it through the inline instance with KaTeX.

cases.name: inline-strikethrough
cases.about: An answer with no formula, so it takes the inline instance without KaTeX, which most answers do; its GFM strikethrough holds that instance to gfm by its output.
